newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines 91-day treasury bill rate up.
newsitem.headline: Philippines 91-day treasury bill rate up.

text.p: The Philippines' benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate rose to an average of 11.536 percent at Monday's weekly regular auction from 11.330, the Bureau of Treasury said.
The 182-day bill rate likewise moved up to an average of 11.937 percent from last week's 11.716; and the 364-day bill increased to 12.845 percent from 12.585.
Traders said the higher yield fetched by the latest auction mirrored the current tightness in the overnight market. Banks had invested their pesos heavily in reverse repos.
A foreign bank dealer said a technical rally in interest rates was expected after almost four weeks of declines.
"Banks are wary. A drop in interest rates usually accompany speculation in the foreign exchange," the same dealer said.
Moreover, some banks have held off from the auction to prepare for Tuesday's maiden offer of the fixed-rate, ten-year Treasury bonds, one dealer said.

The auction drew total tenders of 6.095 billion pesos, of which 4.80 billion pesos were awarded. The government had targeted to sell 6.0 billion pesos worth of bills but had to reject some bids due to their high rates, traders said.
The 91-day bill generated the most interest with bids amounting to 2.160 billion pesos, of which 1.500 billion pesos were sold.
The 182-day bills had 1.975 billion pesos of tenders with 1.800 billion pesos awarded.
And the 364-day bills, of which 1.500 billion pesos were sold, had bids worth 1.960 billion pesos.
